report.name: FINREP F18.04 — Impairment & Credit Risk
report.description: Quarterly impairment and exposure disclosure for the loan portfolio. Figures are built from the core-banking loan book through an IFRS 9 expected-credit-loss engine and aggregated by segment.

table.caption: F18.04 — Accumulated impairment by portfolio segment (reporting period 2026-Q3)

cdes.aggregation_level: Portfolio segment (SUM of account-level lifetime ECL)
cdes.definition: Total loan-loss allowance recognised under IFRS 9 across all stages, aggregated over the portfolio.

candidates.why: Final regulatory output dataset; column name and report mapping match the F18.04 cell.
Aggregation mart one hop upstream — same column name but not the published report layer.
Account-level ECL before segment aggregation; different grain and column name.

cdes.expected_story: Reported allowance = SUM of account lifetime ECL by segment. Each account's lifetime ECL is scenario-weighted EAD × PD × LGD × discount, computed in SAS. The field-level trace crosses SQL → SAS → SQL.

cdes.definition: Accumulated impairment divided by gross carrying amount (total exposure) for the segment.

candidates.why: Ratio computed in the aggregation mart; report multiplies by 100.
Report-layer percentage form; derived directly from the mart ratio.

cdes.expected_story: coverage_ratio = SUM(lifetime_ecl) / SUM(ead). A ratio of two aggregated figures.

cdes.aggregation_level: Account level (derived), summed to segment on the report
cdes.definition: Expected gross exposure at the point of default: drawn balance plus the credit-converted undrawn commitment.

candidates.why: EAD is derived here from balance and undrawn commitment; fully traceable in SQL.

cdes.expected_story: ead_eur = current_balance + undrawn_commitment × credit_conversion_factor. A fully-traceable SQL calculation from raw fields.

cdes.definition: Twelve-month probability of default taken from the rating model and carried through the loan book.

candidates.why: Direct rename of the rating-model PD; one-to-one source mapping.

cdes.expected_story: pd is a direct rename of raw.loan_accounts.pd_12m — a one-to-one source mapping.

cdes.definition: Mean probability of default per segment, used to back-test the rating model.

candidates.why: Produced by a Python groupby; the field-level trace is opaque until the AI layer reads the aggregation.

cdes.expected_story: avg_pd = mean(pd) grouped by segment, computed in Python. The field-level trace stops at the Python boundary until the AI layer reads the groupby.

code.text:
-- Core banking: loan master (system of record)
CREATE TABLE raw.loan_accounts (
  loan_id                   VARCHAR PRIMARY KEY,
  current_balance_eur       DECIMAL(18,2),
  undrawn_commitment_eur    DECIMAL(18,2),
  credit_conversion_factor  DECIMAL(5,4),
  pd_12m                    DECIMAL(9,6),
  lgd_downturn              DECIMAL(9,6),
  rating_grade              VARCHAR,
  segment_code              VARCHAR
);

-- Collateral management system
CREATE TABLE raw.collateral (
  loan_id              VARCHAR,
  collateral_type      VARCHAR,
  collateral_value_eur DECIMAL(18,2),
  haircut_pct          DECIMAL(5,4)
);

-- IFRS 9 forward-looking macro scenario set
CREATE TABLE risk.macro_scenarios (
  scenario_id     VARCHAR,
  scenario_weight DECIMAL(5,4),
  gdp_shock       DECIMAL(9,6),
  hpi_shock       DECIMAL(9,6)
);

-- 01_stage_loan_book.sql  ·  build the staged loan book
CREATE TABLE stg.loan_book AS
SELECT
    a.loan_id,
    a.current_balance_eur,
    a.undrawn_commitment_eur,
    -- Exposure at default = drawn + CCF-weighted undrawn
    a.current_balance_eur
      + a.undrawn_commitment_eur * a.credit_conversion_factor AS ead_eur,
    a.pd_12m       AS pd,
    a.lgd_downturn AS lgd,
    a.segment_code AS segment
FROM raw.loan_accounts a;

-- net collateral after regulatory haircut
CREATE TABLE stg.collateral AS
SELECT
    loan_id,
    collateral_value_eur * (1 - haircut_pct) AS net_collateral_eur
FROM raw.collateral;

# 05_pd_backtest.py  ·  PD model back-test (segment means)
import pandas as pd

loan_book = pd.read_sql("SELECT segment, pd FROM stg.loan_book", conn)

pd_backtest = (
    loan_book
      .groupby("segment", as_index=False)
      .agg(avg_pd=("pd", "mean"),
           n_accounts=("pd", "size"))
)
pd_backtest.to_sql("pd_backtest", conn, if_exists="replace")

-- 03_impairment_mart.sql  ·  aggregate ECL to portfolio segment
CREATE TABLE mart.impairment_by_segment AS
SELECT
    b.segment,
    SUM(e.lifetime_ecl_eur)             AS accumulated_impairment_eur,
    SUM(b.ead_eur)                      AS ead_total_eur,
    SUM(e.lifetime_ecl_eur)
      / NULLIF(SUM(b.ead_eur), 0)       AS coverage_ratio
FROM work.ecl_by_account e
JOIN stg.loan_book b ON e.loan_id = b.loan_id
GROUP BY b.segment;

-- 04_finrep_f1804_report.sql  ·  FINREP F18.04 template
CREATE TABLE finrep_f1804_impairment AS
SELECT
    segment                        AS report_row,
    ead_total_eur                  AS gross_carrying_amount_eur,
    accumulated_impairment_eur,
    ROUND(coverage_ratio * 100, 2) AS coverage_ratio_pct
FROM mart.impairment_by_segment;

tableEdges.reason: Lifetime ECL is computed inside the SAS %ecl_engine macro (scenario-weighted EAD × PD × LGD × discount). The parser resolves the inputs at table level but cannot read the per-column formula inside the macro — this is where AI + a manual review of run logs and the model catalogue close the gap.
Collateral feeds the same SAS ECL engine; the LGD adjustment happens inside the macro and is opaque to static parsing.
Forward-looking scenarios are cross-joined and weighted inside the SAS macro; the weighting logic is not statically visible.
avg_pd is produced by a pandas groupby().agg() in Python. The aggregation is opaque to the static parser until the AI layer reads the Python.
